## Problem

The shipped Kanbus cloud foundation (`KanbusCloudFoundation` in `infra/cloud`) keeps a NAT Gateway running 24/7. That idle floor dominates Kanbus AWS spend even when the console is barely used.

## Why it costs so much

`cloud_stack.py` creates a VPC with `nat_gateways=1` and places the console Lambda and EFS in `PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS` subnets. Private-subnet Lambdas need NAT (or VPC endpoints) to reach AWS APIs and the internet. A NAT Gateway bills hourly plus data processing whether or not anyone is using Kanbus.

In account `335163751677` (`us-east-1`), August 2026 Cost Explorer unblended cost for NAT `nat-06056a113e469e372` was about **$33.48**. The gateway has been up since 2026-03-07. That is one of the largest lines on a ~$193 August bill. Public IPv4 on the NAT adds more.

This is an architecture tax, not usage. Traffic-related Lambda and API Gateway charges are small next to the always-on NAT.

## Suggested direction (not this ticket)

Chatticus already avoided this pattern. Its Computers VPC uses `natGateways: 0` and public subnets only. Fargate `desiredCount` defaults to 0. There is no load balancer. August Chatticus Fargate was about $0.06.

Treat the Chatticus cloud design as the alternative to study: scale-to-zero idle floor, no NAT, no ALB hourly charge. Re-architecting Kanbus cloud, or implementing that alternative, is out of scope for filing this bug.

## Expected later outcome

Kanbus cloud should not pay a ~$30+/month NAT idle floor when the product is idle. A later issue or epic can choose how (Chatticus-style public subnets, VPC endpoints, or tearing the foundation down until it is needed).

## Implementation Plan: S3 Bridge Sync (No NAT)

### Decision locked
Two-Lambda + S3 bridge. No Fargate, no ECS, no CodeBuild, no ALB, no NAT Gateway, no NAT instance, no VPC interface endpoints. ConsoleLambda stays on EFS unchanged. Git sync keeps working.

### Why
EFS forces compute into a VPC. VPC compute without NAT cannot reach GitHub (Lambda and CodeBuild ENIs get no public IP). The S3 bridge splits the job so no single compute needs both internet and EFS. S3 gateway endpoint is free (no hourly, no per-GB).

### Architecture

1. **Git Sync Lambda (non-VPC, new)** — consumes existing SyncQueue. Does git clone --no-checkout / git fetch / git reset --hard to /tmp, tars the repo, uploads tarball to S3. No VPC, no EFS, free internet.
2. **S3 bucket (new)** — stores tenant repo tarballs keyed {account}/{project}/{sha}.tar.gz. Lifecycle: expire after 7 days. SSE-S3.
3. **S3 gateway endpoint (free)** — vpc.add_gateway_endpoint so VPC-isolated Lambdas can read S3 without NAT.
4. **EFS Writer Lambda (VPC, isolated, EFS, new)** — triggered by S3 object-created. Downloads tarball from S3 via gateway endpoint, extracts to EFS at /mnt/data/{account}/{project}/repo, publishes IoT cloud_sync_completed. VPC-isolated, no internet, no NAT.
5. **ConsoleLambda (VPC, isolated, EFS, existing)** — unchanged. Reads EFS as today.
6. **Delete** TenantSyncWorker Lambda + sync_worker.Dockerfile in the same changeset.
7. **Leave alone:** webhook, token admin, MQTT authorizer (already not in VPC).

### VPC
nat_gateways=0. Public subnets (unused by compute) + PRIVATE_ISOLATED subnets (ConsoleLambda + EFS Writer Lambda + EFS). No PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS.

### Files
- infra/cloud/kanbus_cloud/cloud_stack.py — VPC/subnet/SG rework; ConsoleLambda to isolated; remove TenantSyncWorker; add S3 bucket + lifecycle; add S3 gateway endpoint; add Git Sync Lambda (non-VPC) + EFS Writer Lambda (VPC isolated EFS); wire SQS to Git Sync Lambda; wire S3 event to EFS Writer Lambda; update alarms/outputs.
- infra/cloud/lambda/sync_git_lib.py (new) — shared git + tarball helpers, no boto3, importable by tests.
- infra/cloud/lambda/sync_git.py (new) — Git Sync Lambda handler, non-VPC, SQS to S3.
- infra/cloud/lambda/sync_git.Dockerfile (new) — git binary for Git Sync Lambda.
- infra/cloud/lambda/sync_efs_writer.py (new) — EFS Writer Lambda handler, VPC isolated, S3 to EFS, IoT publish.
- infra/cloud/lambda/sync_worker.py (delete)
- infra/cloud/lambda/sync_worker.Dockerfile (delete)
- infra/cloud/tests/test_no_nat_idle_cost.py (new) — zero NatGateway, zero ALB, zero ECS, TenantSyncWorker removed, Git Sync not in VPC, EFS Writer in VPC isolated with EFS, S3 gateway endpoint present, S3 bucket with lifecycle, SQS triggers Git Sync, S3 triggers EFS Writer.
- infra/cloud/tests/test_ops_guardrails.py (modify) — alarm updates.
- infra/cloud/tests/test_sync_handlers.py (modify) — tests for both new Lambdas.
- infra/cloud/README.md, docs/CLOUD_OPS_RUNBOOK.md, docs/CLOUD_CONSOLE_RUNTIME.md, docs/CLOUD_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md, scripts/cloud/validate_preacceptance.sh (modify) — sync path wording, no Fargate/CodeBuild mentions.

### Cutover
Single atomic CDK deploy. Delete TenantSyncWorker + add two new Lambdas + S3 bucket + gateway endpoint in one changeset. One SQS consumer (Git Sync Lambda). One S3 trigger (EFS Writer Lambda). No dual actors.

### Tests
- test_zero_nat_gateways
- test_zero_alb_nlb
- test_zero_ecs_resources
- test_tenant_sync_worker_removed
- test_git_sync_lambda_not_in_vpc
- test_efs_writer_lambda_in_vpc_isolated_with_efs
- test_s3_gateway_endpoint_present
- test_sync_bucket_lifecycle_seven_day_expiration
- test_sqs_triggers_git_sync_lambda_only
- test_s3_object_created_triggers_efs_writer_lambda
- test_efs_security_group_restricts_nfs_to_console_and_writer

### Staging smoke
Deploy KanbusCloudFoundation (AWS_PROFILE=anthus, account 335163751677). No --all, no main. Verify: no NAT on VPC, /api/auth/bootstrap 200, ConsoleLambda logs appear, webhook to SQS to Git Sync to S3 to EFS Writer to EFS to IoT cloud_sync_completed. DLQ empty.

### Out of scope
Fargate, ECS, CodeBuild, ALB/NLB, NAT Gateway, NAT instance, VPC interface endpoints, changes to console_lambda.rs, merge to main, cdk deploy --all.

### Worktree
/tmp/kanbus-kbs-3b5cc3-s3-bridge on branch fix/kbs-3b5cc3-s3-bridge from origin/develop. PR to develop only.
